summary.headline: Start with a narrowly scoped paid service; turn repeated delivery into software later.
summary.best_opportunity: Workflow automation implementation and monthly support for a single SME niche
summary.why_now: The 2025 UK business-population release counts 5.7 million private-sector businesses, including 5.64 million small firms, while the 2025 cyber survey reports 43% of businesses experienced a breach or attack. These establish a broad SMB base and operational pain, not proven willingness to buy automation; validate with paid pilots.

top_opportunities.name: Niche SME workflow automation service
top_opportunities.description: Sell one fixed-scope workflow improvement, such as enquiry triage, quote follow-up or document processing, using existing tools and human review; charge setup plus support.
top_opportunities.why_now: Large small-business base and accessible low-code/AI tools make service delivery practical without building a product. Official business counts are context, not demand validation.
top_opportunities.buyer: Owner-managed trades, recruiters or professional-services firms handling repetitive inbound enquiries and admin.
top_opportunities.startup_cost: £100–£600 for software, domain, outreach and pilot delivery; well below the £2,000 cap.
top_opportunities.speed_to_revenue: 1–3 weeks is plausible with direct outreach and a paid pilot; not guaranteed.
top_opportunities.recurring_revenue: Setup fee plus roughly £100–£500/month for monitoring, adjustments and support, subject to demonstrated ongoing value.
top_opportunities.founder_fit: Very strong: technical delivery, low capital requirement and scope can be constrained part-time.
risks: SMEs may not pay or may have poorly defined processes; secure a paid pilot before building reusable software.
Personal data, vendor dependence and integration failures require access controls, human review and clear service terms.
top_opportunities.verdict: Best near-term choice: sell an outcome first, then standardise only what customers repeatedly buy.

top_opportunities.name: Lead-capture and conversion refresh for local service firms
top_opportunities.description: Fixed-price landing-page and enquiry-flow refresh with call/form tracking, speed and mobile fixes, optionally followed by maintenance and monthly reporting.
top_opportunities.why_now: Easy to demonstrate specific website friction and pitch directly; demand for any particular redesign is not established by general business counts.
top_opportunities.buyer: Local trades and appointment-based service firms whose sites make contacting them difficult or do not track enquiries.
top_opportunities.startup_cost: £100–£800 using existing templates, hosting and analytics.
top_opportunities.speed_to_revenue: 1–4 weeks; deposits can fund a tightly scoped delivery.
top_opportunities.recurring_revenue: £50–£250/month for updates, hosting and reporting; do not guarantee lead volume.
top_opportunities.founder_fit: Strong engineering fit; requires consistent prospecting and a niche to avoid generic-agency competition.
risks: Crowded market and price pressure for generic web builds.
Client outcomes depend on traffic, offer and sales follow-up as well as site quality.
top_opportunities.verdict: A sensible fallback when paired with enquiry handling and measurable conversion fixes.

top_opportunities.name: SME cyber-hygiene setup and maintenance
top_opportunities.description: A non-certification, bounded service to configure MFA, review account access, check backups and produce a simple action register; refer specialist work onward.
top_opportunities.why_now: DSIT's 2025 survey says 43% of businesses reported a breach or attack in the prior 12 months, including phishing as the most common type. This supports risk awareness, not direct demand for this service.
top_opportunities.buyer: Microbusinesses and small professional firms without an internal IT/security lead.
top_opportunities.startup_cost: £200–£1,000 for training, secure tooling, insurance and outreach; verify insurance and competence before offering.
top_opportunities.speed_to_revenue: 2–6 weeks; trust and scope definition may slow sales.
top_opportunities.recurring_revenue: £75–£300/month for access reviews, backup checks and staff reminders, only within demonstrated competence.
top_opportunities.founder_fit: Good technical fit but requires security discipline, appropriate insurance and clear limits; avoid claiming certification.
risks: High liability and trust burden; errors can worsen security or create client harm.
Official breach prevalence does not prove small firms will buy an external review.
top_opportunities.verdict: Promising only with competence, insurance and a tightly bounded non-certification offer.

top_opportunities.name: Productized CRM and follow-up setup
top_opportunities.description: Configure a lightweight CRM, pipeline, reminders and simple reporting for a single niche; charge for setup and monthly administration or improvement.
top_opportunities.why_now: A concrete follow-up process can be sold as an operational fix without developing SaaS; validate that prospects currently lose or delay enquiries.
top_opportunities.buyer: Small B2B service providers or trades with several active leads and inconsistent follow-up.
top_opportunities.startup_cost: £100–£500 using client-owned or low-cost CRM accounts and standard integrations.
top_opportunities.speed_to_revenue: 1–4 weeks after identifying a buyer with visible pipeline pain.
top_opportunities.recurring_revenue: £100–£400/month for reporting, workflow tuning and data hygiene where ongoing work is valued.
top_opportunities.founder_fit: Strong fit for a software engineer who can integrate tools; requires discovery and process coaching.
risks: Clients may not maintain CRM data, reducing measurable value and retention.
Many CRM consultants compete; niche and fixed scope are essential.
top_opportunities.verdict: Sell a working pipeline outcome, not generic CRM configuration.

top_opportunities.name: Micro-SaaS for one repeated back-office task
top_opportunities.description: Build a narrow tool only after paid service work reveals a frequent, costly workflow and several buyers confirm the same requirements.
top_opportunities.why_now: Service-led discovery can reduce wasted build effort; available public evidence here does not establish demand for a specific SaaS niche.
top_opportunities.buyer: A narrowly defined UK trade or professional niche with a repeated admin task and existing spend or manual workaround.
top_opportunities.startup_cost: £300–£2,000 for a lean prototype, hosting and basic legal/privacy work, excluding founder time.
top_opportunities.speed_to_revenue: Usually slower than services; 4–12+ weeks is possible after validation, but uncertain.
top_opportunities.recurring_revenue: Subscription potential, but retention and acquisition economics are unproven until users pay and keep using it.
top_opportunities.founder_fit: Strong build fit, weaker immediate-cash fit; part-time scope must stay very small.
risks: Building before finding committed buyers can consume the full budget without revenue.
Support, compliance and customer acquisition may exceed part-time capacity.
top_opportunities.verdict: Do not start here; earn and learn through paid implementation before productising.

best_pick.name: Niche SME workflow automation service
best_pick.why_it_wins: Fastest credible route to paid validation under £2,000: sell a measurable workflow outcome with existing tools, and only productise repeated demand. UK official statistics show a large small-business base, but neither source proves willingness to pay for automation.
validation_plan: Choose one reachable niche and interview 10 owners about a recent missed enquiry or repetitive workflow; record current cost, frequency and tools.
Offer a fixed-price, human-reviewed pilot to 3 qualified prospects; proceed only if at least one pays and the result is measurable.
best_pick.first_offer: £300–£750 setup for one workflow (for example, enquiry capture plus follow-up reminders), with a separately priced £100–£250/month monitoring and improvement option; final pricing must be tested with buyers.
best_pick.mvp: A single documented workflow using the client's existing systems, with exception alerts, human approval, a basic outcome log and rollback/manual fallback; no standalone SaaS.
customer_types: Owner-managed local trades receiving web or phone enquiries
Small recruiters or professional-services firms processing repetitive inbound requests
best_pick.do_today: Pick one reachable niche, draft a one-page paid-pilot offer, and contact 10 owners with a specific question about their current enquiry/admin bottleneck.
